instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Admit You Need Me
cards.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put on goggles like you. This cupboard clearly needs two specialists. You can say you need me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: These are reading glasses. I'm looking for the hinge diagram.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Close-detail work. I'll keep mine on while you find our diagram.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Found it. Hold the door upright while I screw it on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Upright, naturally. Set it where you want it, then tell me you couldn't do this without me.

beats.text: I'm rolling them up to wash my hands. I'm the pianist.

cards.title: Don’t Go
cards.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned my bowl upside down like yours. Before you leave the class, we ought to finish this stage together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's upside down to dry. The cooking's finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the drying stage. You can check mine before you go; I wouldn't rush a finish like this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is plastic. Wipe it with a towel and pack it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the towel finish. You fold yours so neatly—show me that fold with mine, then we're done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stacked my game pieces like yours. Before you go, we should play out this last formation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's how they fit in the box. The game's over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The closing formation. We should put mine away in the same order as yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just tip them in. They all fit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, one decisive move. You do the first handful and I'll match it; we don't want to spoil the finish.

cards.title: Say You’re Sorry
cards.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're standing, so I'll stand too. Before we make the dinner speeches, there's something I'd like you to say to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm stretching my leg. There aren't any speeches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Just a few private words, then. Something that would let us sit down happy with each other.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you're upset. Can we sit now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly. You said that so confidently—try it again with what you're sorry for, rather than how I feel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've pressed mute, so I've muted mine. Before the presentation, this seems a good moment for you to say something to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's muted because it's feeding back. Yours wasn't even on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Better to be ahead of it. We've got a quiet moment now; I'd like to hear that you're sorry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about the microphone. Shall I switch yours on?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Leave it off for one more sentence, though. The microphone isn't what I need you to be sorry about.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You raised your auction paddle so decisively that I raised mine. You'll agree the wardrobe I just bought is a good choice?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was scratching my ear. You've spent our sofa money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. An opening move on storage. You'll agree it will be useful in the bedroom?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We needed somewhere to sit, not somewhere to put clothes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Put the clothes from our chairs into it. Can we call the seating problem solved and keep the wardrobe?

beats.text: You moved your name card to this table, so I moved mine beside it. You'll agree I should sit here now?

beats.text: I'm the waiter. That card says reserved, not my name.

beats.text: The whole table's reserved for the choir. Are you singing?

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said these invitations need bleeding, so I've brought a red pen. Eighty envelopes still need lettering; that could be your special part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Bleed means printing past the edge. I'm not writing eighty addresses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, past the edge. I'll read the addresses; you could do those sweeping letters you used on the sample.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a font on my computer. I'd print labels if someone peeled them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, the digital lettering. I'll peel every one. Would you take charge of making them look like that sample?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put all the black chess pieces on one tray, so I've done the same. You'd enjoy sorting the club cupboard—pick the best set for yourself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm cleaning one color at a time. A set needs both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Cleaning first. Once the sets are ready, you could choose whichever you like.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're identical. I'd do it if you'd finally play me next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, choose the opponent, not the set. Sort the cupboard and you've got me next week. I'll play whichever color you leave me.
